topLine: One Nation dominated NSW state political coverage, with the Sydney Morning Herald reporting a growing list of former Coalition MPs seeking spots on the party's upper house ticket and leader Mike Newman making a surprise appearance at state parliament before challenging Premier Chris Minns to a debate in the Hunter. In policy, the Minns government announced interim state-funded aged care services to move "stranded" older patients out of hospital, extended toll relief to more than 200,000 additional motorists, and the Federal Court set aside the Commonwealth heritage protection order that had stalled the McPhillamys goldmine in central-west NSW. Election analyst Ben Raue also published fresh seat-level modelling from DemosAU's latest MRP poll.

briefing.topLine: One Nation dominated NSW state political coverage, with the Sydney Morning Herald reporting a growing list of former Coalition MPs seeking spots on the party's upper house ticket and leader Mike Newman making a surprise appearance at state parliament before challenging Premier Chris Minns to a debate in the Hunter. In policy, the Minns government announced interim state-funded aged care services to move "stranded" older patients out of hospital, extended toll relief to more than 200,000 additional motorists, and the Federal Court set aside the Commonwealth heritage protection order that had stalled the McPhillamys goldmine in central-west NSW. Election analyst Ben Raue also published fresh seat-level modelling from DemosAU's latest MRP poll.
briefing.localWatch: Shoalhaven City Council is consulting on paid parking for visitors, with exemptions proposed for eligible local households, while the Illawarra Mercury reports the new November train timetable will lengthen trips to Sydney. Shellharbour Hospital has started a short-stay surgery service aimed at regional elective surgery waiting lists.

stories.headline: Free for locals, fee for tourists? Shoalhaven seeks public say on new idea
stories.summary: Shoalhaven City Council is seeking community feedback on a proposal to charge visitors for parking, with revenue reported as going towards roadworks. The South Coast Register reports eligible local households could apply for two free vehicle exemptions, and the council has opened a public consultation.

stories.headline: Longer trip to Sydney, no Wolli Creek, but more frequent trains: new timetable revealed
stories.summary: The Illawarra Mercury reports that journeys to Sydney will take longer under the new train timetable starting in November, which also drops Wolli Creek but adds more frequent services. The paper reports the change is worse again for commuters who park at Waterfall.

stories.headline: Shellharbour Hospital's plan to fast-track surgeries and ease region waitlist times
stories.summary: The Illawarra Mercury reports Shellharbour Hospital has introduced a high-volume short-stay surgery service under a NSW government plan to reduce elective surgery waiting lists across the region.

stories.headline: The long list of former Coalition MPs seeking new home on One Nation’s crowded NSW ticket
stories.summary: The Sydney Morning Herald reports One Nation has yet to confirm most of its candidates for the coming NSW election, but that possible nominees include a growing number of former Liberal and Nationals MPs along with past political aspirants.

stories.headline: Newman challenges Minns to Hunter debate
stories.summary: The Newcastle Herald reports One Nation leader Mike Newman has challenged Premier Chris Minns to a debate in the Hunter.

stories.headline: NSW steps further into aged care as report warns state not to replace Commonwealth
stories.summary: The Minns government says it will provide interim aged care services to help older patients who are stuck in hospital return home sooner and more safely. The ABC reports the state's productivity commissioner has called for new approaches to stop the number of "stranded" aged care patients in hospitals growing further, and the government release notes a report warning the state should not take over the Commonwealth's role.

stories.headline: Court overturns Tanya Plibersek’s protection order which stalled controversial NSW goldmine
stories.summary: The Federal Court has overturned the Aboriginal heritage protection order issued in 2024 by then federal environment minister Tanya Plibersek over the McPhillamys goldmine at Blayney in central-west NSW, which the company said had effectively blocked the project. The ABC reports the court found the Commonwealth decision was made without authority, after a challenge by Regis Resources.

stories.headline: More than 200,000 additional NSW motorists can now claim toll relief
stories.summary: 7NEWS reports more than 200,000 extra NSW motorists have become eligible for toll relief, with newly eligible drivers estimated to receive about $520 back over a year.

stories.headline: NSW to waive stamp duty as Chalmers charges ahead on trust changes
stories.summary: The Australian reports NSW will waive stamp duty, as federal Treasurer Jim Chalmers proceeds with changes affecting trusts. Only the headline was available for this item.

stories.headline: Inmate died after waiting 305 days for help, NSW coroner finds
stories.summary: The ABC reports a NSW coroner has found that a lengthy wait for support at a prison where two mental health nurses are responsible for 700 inmates likely contributed to the 2023 death of Alexander Gavranic at Junee Correctional Centre.

stories.headline: Tenders called for Grawin Creek Bridge and Rawsonville Bridge replacements
stories.summary: The state government says tenders are now open for the construction of replacement crossings at Grawin Creek and Rawsonville, two ageing bridges in western NSW.

stories.headline: Jindabyne’s new multi-use biathlon track continues adventure sport boom
stories.summary: The state government has announced a $4.4 million upgrade to training facilities at the Jindabyne Sport and Recreation Centre in the Snowy region, including a new multi-use biathlon track.

stories.headline: Fairer pay for council labour hire workers a step closer
stories.summary: The Minns government says it will introduce legislation to stop council workers engaged through labour hire firms being paid less than they would be if employed directly by the council.

stories.headline: $20m public liability insurance to rally in a park: how council red tape hinders the right to protest
stories.summary: A report by the Australian Democracy Network and Deakin University's Centre for Law as Protection argues council administrative requirements are hampering the right to protest. The Guardian reports the research cites a regional NSW council telling a protest organiser they needed a $20 million public liability insurance policy to hold a rally in a park.

stories.headline: New DemosAU MRP – how a small swing costs a lot of seats
stories.summary: Ben Raue examines the fourth MRP poll DemosAU has published in the past year — large surveys that project a result in every seat — and argues such modelling shows how a modest swing can translate into a large number of seat changes.

stories.headline: One Nation in NSW is starting to feel like a clearing house for bitter exes
stories.summary: In the Sydney Morning Herald, a column argues One Nation's NSW operation is increasingly populated by political castoffs, noting that some within the party are conscious it cannot afford to be seen as a reincarnation of the Liberals.

stories.headline: Crashing question time, backing anti-vax bills: One Nation leader looms large at parliament
stories.summary: The Sydney Morning Herald reports One Nation leader Mike Newman made a surprise visit to NSW parliament, attending question time and watching an upper house speech on an anti-vaccination bill, and assesses his growing presence around the parliament.
